verdicts.evidence: The comparison in s1 supplies isPreinstall, whose uses only suppress response and error logging at f1:80, f1:85, f1:99, f1:107 and f1:112. System information collection and the HTTP and WebSocket sends are outside those conditions.
The condition in s2 controls only console.error for a caught WebSocket import or setup failure. The import and connection creation precede this catch at f1:95-96.
The condition in s3 controls only console.error inside the WebSocket error callback. The send and close operations are in the separate open callback at f1:102-103.
The condition in s4 controls response-body reads used as console.log arguments. Both HTTP requests have already been issued at f1:67 and f1:70, independently of this logging condition.
The condition in s5 controls only the connection-established console.log. The callback sends the data and closes the socket after the conditional at f1:102-103 regardless of isPreinstall.
The condition in s6 controls only console.error for the HTTP failure. The WebSocket fallback call at f1:88 follows the conditional and runs regardless of isPreinstall whenever this catch is entered.
